title: Tool Use, MCP & Streaming
scopeHtml: Scope: the tool-use loop and block pairing rules, schema design, MCP transports and connector, and safe handling of streamed responses.

notes.title: The tool-use loop
notes.html:
The idea. Claude never runs your tools. It reads your tool definitions, decides one fits, and returns a tool_use block (name, unique ID, input) with stop_reason: tool_use. Your code runs the function, then makes a fresh request containing the earlier messages plus a tool_result. The model is stateless between calls; it is not waiting on an open connection.

  1. Define the tools. 2. Send message plus tools. 3. Claude returns tool_use. 4. You execute. 5. You return tool_result (same ID). 6. Claude continues or ends with end_turn.

Real life. A restaurant: the waiter (Claude) writes the order; the kitchen (your code) cooks it; the dish goes back to the table. The waiter does not cook.

Tech. An RPC client that serializes the call; the server (your function) executes and replies.

Key facts

  • Most tool bugs live on the boundary between what Claude owns and what your code owns.
  • Loop until end_turn; the loop is not automatic.

notes.title: Block pairing rules
notes.html:
The idea. Messages are lists of typed blocks: text, tool_use, tool_result, thinking. The hard invariant: every tool_use must be answered by a tool_result with the same ID in the immediately following user turn. Missing, mismatched or late results fail validation. This is structural; no prompt can fix it.

Real life. Every library book borrowed must be matched by a return slip with the same card number, before the next loan. A slip delivered two days later, or with the wrong number, is rejected.

Key facts

  • With several parallel calls, results may come back out of order; the ID links them.
  • A tool that fails still gets a tool_result with is_error: true.
  • Keep the whole content array (including a text block beside tool_use) when you append the turn to history.

notes.title: Writing tool schemas
notes.html:
The idea. A tool has a name, a description and an input_schema. Claude chooses a tool almost entirely from the description.

  • Name: specific (get_account_balance, not get_data).
  • Description: what it does, when to use it, when not to, what it returns (3 to 4 sentences, with sample inputs where format matters).
  • required only for fields the call truly needs; marking everything required forces Claude to invent values.
  • Overlapping tools: add exclusion language to both; if you still cannot separate them, merge into one tool with a type parameter.
  • Independent calls can run in parallel (the default); dependent calls must be separate turns. disable_parallel_tool_use forces one per turn.
  • Over-tooling hurts routing. Start with the minimum set.

Real life. Two light switches both labelled "lights". Add "hallway only" and "everything except hallway" and nobody guesses wrong.

Tech. Two REST endpoints with identical docs: clients call the wrong one until the docs say when each applies.

Key facts

  • Exclusion rules that depend on earlier turns silently fail if history is truncated.

notes.title: MCP
notes.html:
The idea. The Model Context Protocol moves tool definitions and execution into a server. Your MCP client sends ListToolsRequest, passes the definitions to Claude, executes calls, returns results. The loop is unchanged; only who wrote the tools changes.

Transports. stdio (local subprocess) and Streamable HTTP (remote; POST plus optional SSE stream). SSE-only is deprecated.

API MCP Connector. Remote (HTTP) servers only; beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20. Use an mcp_toolset in tools: default_config, per-tool configs, enabled (allow/deny), defer_loading (load definitions on demand).

Real life. USB-C. Any laptop talks to any charger or monitor because the port is standard; you do not custom-wire each device.

Tech. Language Server Protocol: one protocol, many editors and many language servers.

Key facts

  • Tool definitions cost context even when unused: connect only what you need.
  • Use MCP when a maintained server exists; write schemas yourself for description quality; combine both for breadth and precision.

notes.title: Streaming
notes.html:
The idea. Streaming sends the response as small events. You rebuild the message yourself.

Event You do
message_start create an empty content array
content_block_start open a slot at that index (a tool_use block opens with name and id)
content_block_delta append the fragment (input_json_delta is partial JSON)
content_block_stop finalize; first moment tool JSON can be parsed
message_delta record stop_reason and usage
message_stop message complete: now commit the turn

The rule. Never act on a partial block. Commit the assistant turn to history only after message_stop. On an interrupted stream, throw away the partial turn and retry from the last complete one.

Real life. Watching a download. A half-downloaded file looks like a file but will not open. You only trust it when the progress bar says 100%.

Tech. TCP: you reassemble packets; a connection that dropped mid-message must not be treated as a finished message.

Key facts

  • "The read loop ended" is not "the message is complete".
  • The error appears on the retry request, so teams debug the schema when the cause is the stream.

questions.promptHtml:
Who executes a tool when Claude decides to use it?

  • A. Claude runs the function inside the API and returns the result
  • B. Your application: Claude returns a tool_use block, your code runs the tool and sends back a tool_result in a new request
  • C. Anthropic's servers always run it in a sandbox
  • D. The SDK runs it automatically with no code from you

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. Claude only requests the call. The model is stateless between calls, so you make a fresh request with the prior messages plus the result.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: The response has stop_reason: tool_use. The loop is not automatic: step four (execute) is yours. Server-run tools (like code execution) and Managed Agents are different paths, but for client-defined tools your code owns execution. Most tool bugs live on this boundary.

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Thinking Claude "waits" on an open connection for the result.
  • Forgetting to loop until stop_reason is end_turn.

questions.promptHtml:
In one assistant turn Claude emits three tool_use blocks. Your code returns two tool_result blocks in the next user turn and the third in a later turn. What happens?

  • A. The API accepts it and Claude waits for the third
  • B. The request fails validation: every tool_use must be answered by a tool_result with the same ID in the immediately following user turn
  • C. The third tool call is silently dropped
  • D. Claude re-issues the third call automatically

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. All tool_use blocks from one assistant turn must be resolved together, in the next user turn, with matching IDs.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: This is structural, not promptable. Results can arrive out of order because the ID, not position, links each result to its call. If one tool fails, still return a tool_result for it with is_error: true.

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Running parallel calls and returning only the successful ones.
  • Dropping the text block that arrived with the tool_use when appending to history.

questions.contextHtml: A developer registers search_docs ("Use this to find information about the product") and get_context_summary ("Use this to retrieve relevant information from the current session"). Claude often calls search_docs when the answer is already in the conversation. They have re-run the test four times.
questions.promptHtml:
What is the most effective fix?

  • A. Rename the tools to longer names
  • B. Add an exclusion to both descriptions: when to use each and when not to (e.g. "Do not call if the answer is already in the current session")
  • C. Add "please choose carefully" to the system prompt
  • D. Mark every parameter required

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: Renaming the tools or telling Claude to be careful. The two descriptions are indistinguishable at decision time, so wording elsewhere will not help.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: What are the exact descriptions? Is full history sent every request (exclusion logic relies on it)?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Patch both descriptions with a use-when and a do-not-use-when sentence.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: Overlapping descriptions; truncated history; too many registered tools.
  4. How I'd verify each: Replay the failing prompts with traces of which tool was chosen.
  5. Root cause: Both descriptions say "find information"; routing collapses to description alone.
  6. Fix: B. If the descriptions still cannot be separated, merge into one tool with a type parameter.
  7. Prevention: An eval set of boundary-case inputs for tool selection.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not rely on names alone; not stuff long essays into descriptions, which bury the trigger.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html: • What if history is truncated to save tokens? → The exclusion rule silently fails because Claude can no longer see prior turns.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: blames the model.
  • Hire: adds exclusion conditions.
  • Strong hire: adds exclusions to both, notes the history dependency, proposes a boundary-case eval and the merge option.

questions.promptHtml:
A tool has ten parameters and the author marked all of them required "to be safe". What is the likely production effect?

  • A. Claude refuses to call the tool
  • B. Claude fabricates values for fields it has no basis to fill in
  • C. Claude calls the tool less often but with better inputs
  • D. None; required is only documentation

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. Required means "non-negotiable", so Claude invents values to satisfy it.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Mark a field required only when the call makes no sense without it. Fields with defaults or meaningful absence stay optional so Claude can omit what it does not know. Related: too many tools with overlapping parameters degrade routing, so start with the minimum tool set.

questions.promptHtml:
You want to attach a local filesystem MCP server (stdio) directly to a Messages API request through the MCP connector. What is true?

  • A. The connector supports stdio servers natively
  • B. The connector supports only remote HTTP servers; a stdio server needs you (or Claude Desktop/Claude Code) to act as the MCP client
  • C. Stdio servers are required for remote services
  • D. SSE-only is the recommended transport for new integrations

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. Local servers use stdio (subprocess); remote servers use Streamable HTTP; the API MCP connector handles only the remote kind.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Streamable HTTP uses POST for client→server messages plus an optional GET-based SSE stream; SSE-only is deprecated (D). The connector requires the mcp-client-2025-11-20 beta header and an mcp_toolset entry in tools, where default_config, per-tool configs, enabled (allow/deny) and defer_loading (load definitions on demand) control scope and context cost. Tool definitions cost context even when unused.

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Connecting many servers and burning the window before the first message.
  • Forgetting the beta header, so mcp_toolset settings do not apply.

questions.contextHtml: A streaming agent appends the assistant turn to history when its read loop exits. On a network blip, a stream ends after a tool_use block opened and received part of its JSON but before content_block_stop. The user retries; the retry fails with a validation error pointing at a malformed tool_use block. The team spends an afternoon auditing the tool schema.
questions.promptHtml:
What is the root cause and fix?

  • A. The tool schema is invalid; rewrite it
  • B. "The read loop ended" was treated as "the message is complete"; only message_stop means whole, so gate the history append on it, discard the partial turn and retry from the last complete turn
  • C. Switch to non-streaming permanently
  • D. Parse the partial JSON optimistically and run the tool

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: Debugging the schema or retry logic because the error surfaces on the retry request, not the failed stream.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Was the previous turn built from a stream? Did it end with message_stop?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Drop the half-built assistant turn from stored history.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: Partial block committed; schema bug; ID mismatch.
  4. How I'd verify each: Inspect the stored turn for truncated input JSON.
  5. Root cause: B.
  6. Fix: Accumulate input_json_delta by block index, parse only after content_block_stop, commit the turn after message_stop, check stop_reason before continuing.
  7. Prevention: A fault-injection test that cuts the stream mid-block.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not abandon streaming; it is right for user-facing output.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html: • Is a partial text block as dangerous? → Cosmetic for display, but still do not store it as a complete turn.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: rewrites the schema.
  • Hire: identifies the partial block.
  • Strong hire: gates on message_stop, discards and retries, adds fault-injection tests.

questions.promptHtml:
After Claude returns a tool_use block, what must your next request contain?

  • A. Only the tool result
  • B. The prior messages plus a tool_result for that call
  • C. Nothing; Claude keeps the session open
  • D. A new system prompt

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. The model is stateless between calls, so you resend the conversation plus the result.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: The assistant turn has already ended; Claude is not holding a connection open. Sending only the result (A) loses the context that made the call meaningful.

questions.promptHtml:
Your loop should continue only when which condition holds?

  • A. The response contains any text
  • B. stop_reason is tool_use; it ends on end_turn
  • C. The response is longer than 100 tokens
  • D. Always continue until a timeout

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. tool_use means your tool calls are ready to run; other values are different paths.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Add your own exit conditions (max iterations) so the loop does not depend on Claude volunteering to stop.

questions.promptHtml:
Two independent lookups are needed, and a third call depends on both results. How should this run?

  • A. All three in one turn
  • B. The two independent calls in one turn (parallel), the dependent call in a later turn
  • C. Three separate turns always
  • D. The dependent call first

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. Dependent calls need earlier results, so they go in separate turns.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Current models default to parallel calls when independent. disable_parallel_tool_use forces one call per turn if you need it.

questions.promptHtml:
Which description is best for a balance lookup tool?

  • A. "Use this to find information."
  • B. "Retrieves the current balance for one account ID. Do not use for transaction history. Returns amount and currency."
  • C. "Gets data."
  • D. "Account tool."

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. It says what it does, an exclusion, and what it returns.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Too short and Claude guesses; too long and the trigger is buried. Aim for 3 to 4 sentences with example inputs where format matters.

questions.promptHtml:
Two tools are so similar that even long exclusions cannot separate them. What is the best structural fix?

  • A. Add more exclusions forever
  • B. Merge them into one tool with a type parameter
  • C. Rename both
  • D. Raise the temperature

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. If descriptions cannot be cleanly separated, they are one tool.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Every extra tool increases the surface Claude must reason over, so over-tooling degrades routing.

questions.promptHtml:
Three parallel tool calls finish out of order. How does Claude match results to calls?

  • A. By position in the list
  • B. By tool_use_id
  • C. By tool name
  • D. By timestamp

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. The ID, not order or name, links each result to its call.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Two calls to the same tool would be ambiguous by name. Return all results in the immediately following user turn.

questions.promptHtml:
Five MCP servers are connected, but a task uses one. What is the side effect?

  • A. None
  • B. All tool definitions occupy context even when unused
  • C. Claude calls every tool
  • D. The servers disconnect

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. Register only what you use; defer_loading and enabled reduce the cost.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: In the API connector these live in mcp_toolset (default_config, per-tool configs). The connector needs the mcp-client-2025-11-20 beta header.

questions.promptHtml:
A well-maintained GitHub MCP server exists. You need broad coverage but precise routing on three tools. Best approach?

  • A. Hand-write every GitHub schema
  • B. Connect the MCP server for breadth, allowlist the needed tools, and tune those tools' descriptions
  • C. Avoid MCP
  • D. Connect and expose everything

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. Use both: breadth from the server, precision from allowlisting and description tuning.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Narrowing the tool set and sharpening descriptions are separate levers; use both.

questions.promptHtml:
When is it safe to parse a streamed tool call's input JSON?

  • A. After the first content_block_delta
  • B. After content_block_stop for that block
  • C. After message_start
  • D. Never

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. Tool input arrives as partial JSON across deltas and is only complete once the block closes.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Commit the whole assistant turn to history only after message_stop, and check stop_reason from message_delta before continuing.

questions.promptHtml:
A stream drops mid-response. What should you do?

  • A. Save the partial turn and continue
  • B. Discard the partial assistant turn and retry from the last complete turn
  • C. Parse whatever JSON you have
  • D. Switch to a smaller model

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: B. A half-built turn in history corrupts the next request.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Track completion explicitly: a turn is usable only once message_stop has arrived. A dropped stream is a transient failure, so retry the whole request.
